cues.en: You can probably guess what your next exercise is.
cues.zh: 你大概猜得到下一個練習。

cues.en: Go ahead and try this out.
cues.zh: 實際試試看。

cues.en: Modify the SVDBakeoff script such that it searches for the best hyperparameters to use with SVD.
cues.zh: 修改 SVDBakeOff 指令碼，搜尋 SVD 的最佳超參數。

cues.en: Then, generate top-end recommendations with it, and see how they look.
cues.zh: 接著，用它產生 Top-N 推薦，看看結果。

cues.en: Oh, and if you notice that the SVDTuning.py file included in the course materials, yeah, that's the solution to this exercise.
cues.zh: 如果注意到教材有 SVDTuning.py，沒錯，那就是這個練習的解答。

cues.en: Resist the temptation to look at it unless you really get stuck.
cues.zh: 除非真的卡住，否則忍住，不要偷看。

cues.en: We'll review that file when we come back.
cues.zh: 回來後，我們會一起看那個檔案。

cues.en: So we can briefly take a look at SVDTuning.py file here to see how I went about doing hyperparameter tuning on SVD.
cues.zh: 現在簡單看看 SVDTuning.py，了解我如何替 SVD 調整超參數。

cues.en: You'll see it's mainly the same code we covered in the slides to set up the GridSearchCV object and use it to find the best parameters to set on SVD.
cues.zh: 主要就是投影片介紹過的程式碼：設定 GridSearchCV 物件，用它找出 SVD 最佳參數。

cues.en: We then set up a little bakeoff between SVD using the default parameters and the tuned parameters we learned from GridSearchCV.
cues.zh: 再讓使用預設參數的 SVD，與使用 GridSearchCV 學到的調整後參數的 SVD，進行比較。

cues.en: Here we see the results.
cues.zh: 這裡看到結果。

cues.en: I settled on 20 epochs, a learning rate of .0005 and 50 factors.
cues.zh: 我最後選了 20 個訓練週期、學習率 0.0005，以及 50 個因子。

cues.en: You may have gotten even better results depending on how persistent you were on iterating on the ideal numbers instead of just estimating them like I did.
cues.zh: 如果你不像我只是估計，而是更有耐心迭代尋找理想數值，可能得到更好結果。

cues.en: But we can see that we did indeed get a better RMSE score with these tuned results.
cues.zh: 不過可以看到，調整後的結果，確實有較好的 RMSE。

cues.en: The difference is small, but it did result in very different top-end recommendation results, which is interesting.
cues.zh: 差異很小，但 Top-N 推薦卻非常不同，很有意思。

cues.en: I would consider both of these results good, but they are completely different.
cues.zh: 我認為兩組結果都不錯，但完全不同。

cues.en: For example, Lord of the Rings doesn't turn up at all when using the default parameters of SVD but all three movies of the trilogy bubbled up when we tuned it.
cues.zh: 例如，SVD 預設參數完全沒出現《魔戒》，調整後，三部曲全部都浮現。

cues.en: While the algorithm is probably correct in predicting that user number 85 would love all three of these movies, this is a good example of where results aren't diverse enough.
cues.zh: 演算法預測使用者 85 會喜歡這三部電影，或許是對的；但這也是結果不夠多樣化的好例子。

cues.en: Often, high diversity is a sign of random recommendations that aren't very good, but diversity that's too low can also be a bad thing.
cues.zh: 高多樣性常代表隨機推薦、品質不好，但多樣性太低，也可能是壞事。

cues.en: It would be better to only recommend the first movie in the series in a case like this and free up those other two slots for different titles.
cues.zh: 這種情況最好只推薦系列第一部，空出另外兩個位置，留給不同片名。

cues.en: Sometimes simple little rules like that, don't recommend more than one movie in the same series, can make a difference.
cues.zh: 有時，「同系列不要推薦超過一部」這類簡單規則，就能帶來改變。
